name: Sortable List
description:
Drag to reorder a list, emitting the new position as one event.
A DATA atom, not a domain one: it renders whatever {id, label} pairs it is given and emits a position, so the same atom serves form fields, a shopping run, or any other AUTHORED ordering. There is deliberately no sortable_jobs and no sortable_fields — one named interaction per use case is the drift this vocabulary already has (onFlightClick, onAssign), and it costs a renderer change every time.
The reason it fits a declarative binding model at all is containment: the gesture never reaches the state engine. dragstart/dragover/drop are high-frequency and purely visual; only the DROP publishes, once, through the `onReorder` output wire as {id, order}. That is the same shape the atom renders FROM, so position is derived state rather than a second source of truth — what it emits and what it consumes are one field.
`order` is fractional: a drop takes the midpoint of its two neighbours, so exactly one item changes. Dense re-indexing would rewrite every position on every drag, turning a one-line reviewable diff into a wall of noise, which matters wherever the result is a change someone accepts or reverts.
Use it only where order is AUTHORED. Where order is COMPUTED — a job list ranked by severity then priority — a dragged position becomes a second, competing ordering, and the derivation boundary rule says that ranking belongs to the server.
queries:
show a drag-to-reorder list emitting {id, order} on drop drag to reorder a list, emitting the new position as one event.
a data atom, not a domain one: it renders whatever render a sortable list

name: Photo Grid
description:
A clickable image grid: every tile is both a photo and a row.
Built to close a real gap — data_table has no way to show what a row IS, only what it says about itself, so a photo-driven decision (which wallpaper, which chair) forced a text table plus a separate "View photo" link plus a separate select-then-tap-a-button flow before an action could fire. This atom is the shape that removes all three: the thing you look at and the thing you click are the same element.
Reuses data_table's onRowClick contract exactly — same data-row-json attribute, same _a2uiBindRowClicks binder, same array-wire form for "select AND immediately run an action" in one tap (shipped 2026-08-04 for onRowClick, inherited here for free rather than rebuilt). A DATA atom, not a domain one, same reasoning sortable_list gives for its own genericness: it renders whatever {id, url, ...} objects it is given and fires whatever the caller wired onRowClick to, so the same atom serves a voting board, a photo picker, or a product chooser without a second named atom per use case.
`badge` and `active` exist because a click-driven UI still has to show its OWN state back — a starred tile that does not visibly read as starred after the tap is a button that looks like it did nothing. Both are plain strings/booleans the caller derives server-side (a star count, a "you picked this" flag); the atom does not compute either.
queries:
show a clickable image grid — data-row-json tiles, reuses data_table's onRowClick contract; badge + active show per-tile state a clickable image grid: every tile is both a photo and a row.
built to close a real gap — data_table has no way to render a photo grid

name: Photo Stepper
description:
A full-viewport, one-photo-at-a-time lightbox with prev/next and a vote button per slide — the sibling photo_grid does not cover: reviewing options ONE AT A TIME with full attention, immersively, rather than scanning a grid. Neither replaces the other; pick per use case, or offer both. Renders closed as a compact trigger card (first photo + label); clicking it opens the full takeover.
The takeover itself is a pure-CSS checkbox toggle — the SAME `#checkbox:checked ~ .overlay{display:...}` pattern the `css_modal` atom already uses for its own position:fixed;inset:0 overlay, not a new mechanism. Paging within the open overlay is the SAME pure-CSS radio-input trick the existing `carousel` atom already uses (sibling :checked selectors drive the slide transform) — no JS-tracked index to go stale, and critically, nothing for a live data refresh to disturb: `carousel` never had a live-update wire to worry about, but this atom does, and the radio's own browser-owned :checked state surviving a vote untouched is what stops "vote on photo 12, get silently bounced back to photo 1" from ever being possible in the first place — not a bug that was fixed, a failure mode the design does not have. Same reasoning protects open/closed state: the checkbox is the browser's own state too, so a live update cannot close the overlay out from under you either.
That is also why this atom's live-update path (_a2uiUpdatePhotoStepper) is NOT a rebuild like photo_grid's own _a2uiUpdatePhotoGrid — it patches each slide's badge/vote-button/voter-line IN PLACE, matched by candidate id (not array position), and touches nothing else. Matching by id, specifically, because the typical consumer of this atom (a live vote board) re-sorts its candidate list by vote count on every read while voting is open — so a candidate's position in the incoming array can move the instant ANY vote lands, including the one just cast on the slide currently open; patching by position against a reordered array would silently swap a different candidate's photo/name into the slide the radio's :checked state still has open. A consequence worth knowing before using this atom: because the update path patches EXISTING slide elements rather than creating them, the caller should populate the initial `images` prop with real data at render time (server-side), not rely purely on the `rows` wire to populate an empty first paint — an update arriving before any slide exists to patch has nothing to act on.
Reuses photo_grid's click contract exactly for the vote button (same data-row-json attribute, same generalised [data-row-json] binder in A2UIState.html) — the third consumer of a mechanism built once for data_table's own onRowClick.
queries: show a full-viewport one-at-a-time photo lightbox — opens from a compact trigger card, carousel-style CSS paging, per-slide vote button reusing photo_grid''s click contract, live badge/voter updates patched in place by candidate id so voting never resets position or swaps photos a full-viewport, one-photo-at-a-time lightbox with prev/next and a vote button per slide — the sibling photo_grid does render a photo stepper

name: Preview Frame
description:
An iframe whose `src` is driven by a wire, so picking a value elsewhere on the page re-navigates it CLIENT-SIDE — no server round trip, no paint_result, nothing else on the page repainted.
A DATA atom, same spirit as sortable_list: it renders whatever src it is given and reacts to whatever is wired into it; it has no opinion on what the iframe shows. Meant to sit next to a picker (menu/select) and a StringTemplate primitive that turns the picked value into a URL — e.g. a "preview this before you commit it" panel, where committing is a SEPARATE, ordinary action.
Same-origin only in practice: nothing here relaxes sandboxing. A cross-origin src is subject to the embedded page's own frame-ancestors / X-Frame-Options exactly as any other iframe.

name: Actual Vs Estimate
description:
A quantity carrying BOTH what is known and what is projected, each labelled, neither omittable. A data atom rather than a domain one: cost is only the first instance. The same shape holds for effort (hours worked vs hours estimated), for work items (closed vs open) and for anything else an app tracks with an actual alongside a forecast — which is most things worth tracking.
Exists because that distinction is where composed answers go wrong. Asked "what has this cost", a model resolves the ambiguity by guessing, and on 2026-08-14 presented a EUR300 estimate for unstarted work under the heading "COST". Selection prose can ask it not to; a required-field shape makes it unrepresentable. Both figures are mandatory for exactly that reason.
The contract runs in two directions, which is the point. Upward it constrains what a UI can say. Downward it tells the data layer what it must be able to produce: an app that cannot separate incurred from projected cannot fill this atom, and discovering that is the useful part.
queries: show a one quantity as actual + estimate, both labelled, neither omittable a quantity carrying both what is known and what is projected, each labelled, neither omittable. a data atom rather render a actual vs estimate

name: Motion Timeline
description: A stage of child atoms choreographed on ONE clock, the way a product or launch video is: everything on screen is a pure function of time (seek(t)), so it plays, loops, scrubs, and can be frozen on any frame (open the page with #t=3.2). Children are any atoms, placed in percent of a fixed-size stage (so the composition is identical at every width) and addressed by id; tracks animate them by opacity, x/y, scale, rotate, 3D tilt, blur, wipe, and two custom properties the demo kit listens to (p = progress, step = which caption/nav item); a camera track pans, zooms and tilts the world while layer:"hud" children (captions) stay put. Each key is a DESTINATION: {t, x, ease} means arrive at x at time t using ease, like GSAP .to(); before a property's first key it holds that first value, so an element can be hidden until its first key. Ease is a token name from motion_tokens (expo-out, standard, quart-in-out, overshoot, hold...) or four cubic-bezier numbers; with bpm set, keys take beat instead of t so the piece sits on a grid. Style that reads as designed rather than generated: one orchestrated moment per scene, entrances 600 ms or less on expo-out, on-screen moves on standard, the camera on quart-in-out, a shared motion vector between scenes, restraint over noise by default (no particle bursts, neon glows or bouncy easing on UI; the opt-in expressive options, glow, shine, trails and ripples, are for a film that wants them). Honours prefers-reduced-motion (holds the poster frame; controls still work).

queries: show a one layer band (badge, name, field/note or per-column cells) — normally used inside layer_stack one band of a layer_stack — a badge, the layer name, and either a single field/note pane or one pane per column via render a stack layer

name: Tool Call Card
description: A structured card displaying an AI agent tool invocation — in-flight, completed, or failed. Shows the tool name, execution status badge (running, success, error, pending), elapsed latency, formatted input arguments, and returned result or error message. Essential for agentic run narration, live tool traces, and human inspection of autonomous actions.
queries: show a structured agent tool call card with status, inputs, result, and latency a structured card displaying an ai agent tool invocation — in-flight, completed, or failed. shows the tool name, render a tool call card

name: Scene Stage
description: An animated, looping pan/zoom SVG scene composed from a provenance-verified prop kit (original MIT artwork, each asset pinned by sha256 and restricted to an allowlist of SVG elements). Give a preset and the layout, backdrop, props and motion come from it; or write the layout in full. Props are referenced by id and never as SVG, so the agent cannot introduce script or external references. For a one-off shape use agent_sketchpad; for a diagram use a chart or d2 atom.
queries: show a animated looping SVG scene of a place (53 ready presets) from verified clipart an animated, looping pan/zoom svg scene composed from a provenance-verified prop kit (original mit artwork, each asset render a scene stage

name: Clipart
description: One piece of verified vector clipart from the scene kit, by id, drawn at its own size with an optional variant (for example a person in a hard hat), scale and flip. Themeable colours, original MIT artwork, no external references. Use it as an illustration inside an article, card or slide; use scene_stage when several props should be composed into a moving picture.

name: Swimlane
description: Rows are roles, columns are phases. Each task is a card with a number that gives the order, placed in its role and phase. At most two tasks share a cell. Motion-ready: every moving value reads --p (build progress 0 to 1, default 1) through a per-item --k, so a motion_timeline track on p builds it item by item and the standalone render is the finished picture; reduced motion shows the end state.
queries: show a swimlane: who does which step, in order, across phases rows are roles, columns are phases. each task is a card with a number that gives the order, placed in its role and render a swimlane

name: Treemap
description: Part-to-whole as nested rectangles whose areas show share of the total, laid out by the squarified treemap algorithm (d3-hierarchy treemapSquarify). By default up to four categories: each category is one block and its items are rectangles inside it, with the category name and total in a pill. With an optional per-item path (1 to 3 group names, top down) the chart nests by that path instead, up to three levels of group boxes with a header showing the group name and total, so a folder tree or a cost breakdown reads like a disk-usage map. Each rectangle carries its name and value where the drawn width and height can hold them; in a narrower container or a thin cell the label is hidden (the hover title and the hidden table keep it). A hidden table gives item, category (or path), value and share. Motion-ready: every moving value reads --p (build progress 0 to 1, default 1) through a per-item --k, so a motion_timeline track on p builds it item by item and the standalone render is the finished picture; reduced motion shows the end state.
queries: show a treemap: part-to-whole by category or nested path part-to-whole as nested rectangles whose areas show share of the total, laid out by the squarified treemap algorithm render a treemap

name: Venn Diagram
description: Two circles with the first set, the shared items and the second set, up to four items each; or, when set_c_name is given, three fixed circles with items in all seven regions (each set alone, each pair, all three). Motion-ready: every moving value reads --p (build progress 0 to 1, default 1) through a per-item --k, so a motion_timeline track on p builds it item by item and the standalone render is the finished picture; reduced motion shows the end state.
queries: show a venn diagram: what two or three sets share two circles with the first set, the shared items and the second set, up to four items each; or, when set_c_name is render a venn diagram

name: Org Chart
description: A hierarchy built from a list of nodes with parents, drawn as boxes in tiers joined by connector lines (layout "tree", the default), as a dendrogram with every leaf on the last tier (layout "cluster"), or as a radial tree with the root at the centre and rotated labels (layout "radial"). It is a real nested list in every layout, so it reads in order to a screen reader. Motion-ready: every moving value reads --p (build progress 0 to 1, default 1) through a per-item --k, so a motion_timeline track on p builds it item by item and the standalone render is the finished picture; reduced motion shows the end state.
queries: show a org chart: a bounded tree of up to thirty nodes, as tiers, a dendrogram or a radial tree a hierarchy built from a list of nodes with parents, drawn as boxes in tiers joined by connector lines (layout "tree", render a org chart

name: Histogram
description: The distribution of a list of numbers: bars of counts per bin on a counted y axis, with the bin edges on the x axis. The bins and the rounded axis come from d3-array bin() with the Sturges rule, computed on the server, so there is no script. A hidden table gives each bin from, to and count. Motion-ready: every moving value reads --p (build progress 0 to 1, default 1) through a per-item --k, so a motion_timeline track on p grows the bars one after another and the standalone render is the finished picture; reduced motion shows the end state.
queries: show a histogram: counts of numbers per bin the distribution of a list of numbers: bars of counts per bin on a counted y axis, with the bin edges on the x axis render a histogram

name: Box Plot
description: Compares groups of numbers as box plots on one shared horizontal axis: per group a box from the lower to the upper quartile, a line at the median, whiskers to the furthest numbers within 1.5 times the box length, and dots for the outliers beyond. The quartiles come from d3-array quantileSorted and the axis from d3 nice() and ticks(), computed on the server, so there is no script. A hidden table gives each group's count, minimum, quartiles, median, maximum and outlier count. Motion-ready: each group fades in through --k from --p (build progress 0 to 1, default 1); the standalone render is the finished picture and reduced motion shows the end state.
queries: show a box_plot: compare groups of numbers by median and spread compares groups of numbers as box plots on one shared horizontal axis: per group a box from the lower to the upper render a box plot

name: Waterfall
description: A running total built step by step, as horizontal bars on one shared axis: each change runs from where the previous step ended (green up, red down) and a total runs from 0 to the running total; dashed connectors join the steps and the signed change is printed at the end of each row, so the direction never rests on colour alone. The axis comes from d3 nice() and ticks(), computed on the server, so there is no script. A hidden table gives each change and the running total. Motion-ready: each step fades in through --k from --p (build progress 0 to 1, default 1); the standalone render is the finished picture and reduced motion shows the end state.
queries: show a waterfall: how changes add up to a total a running total built step by step, as horizontal bars on one shared axis: each change runs from where the previous render a waterfall

name: Sunburst
description: Part-to-whole as nested rings: each item is an arc whose angle shows its share of the total, the top-level groups sit in the innermost ring and each level of the optional per-item path (1 to 3 group names, top down) is one ring further out, so a budget, a disk-usage breakdown or a folder tree reads from the inside out. Laid out by d3-hierarchy partition() and drawn with d3-shape arc() paths on the server, so there is no script. With the optional layout "icicle" the same hierarchy is drawn as horizontal bars instead, the top-level groups in the left column and each level one column further right. A group's hue follows its top-level group and each ring out is a lighter shade of it; every arc or bar carries its name, path, value and share in a hover title and in the hidden table (item, path, value, share of total), and the aria label gives the total, the number of groups and the largest group. Labels are drawn only where they fit and are rotated to read outward, never upside down; the centre of the ring shows the total. Motion-ready: every moving value reads --p (build progress 0 to 1, default 1) through a per-ring --k, so a motion_timeline track on p builds it ring by ring from the inside out and the standalone render is the finished picture; reduced motion shows the end state.
queries: show a sunburst: share of a total in nested rings part-to-whole as nested rings: each item is an arc whose angle shows its share of the total, the top-level groups sit render a sunburst

name: Chord Diagram
description: Flows between a few entities in both directions as a circle: each group is an arc on the ring (its length is the flow that leaves it) and each ribbon joins two groups, its width at each end showing the flow from that group to the other, so migration between regions, traffic between services or trade between countries reads at a glance. Laid out by d3-chord chord() with sorted subgroups and drawn with d3-shape arc() and d3-chord ribbon() paths on the server, so there is no script. With the optional directed true the same matrix is laid out by chordDirected() and every flow is an arrow (ribbonArrow()) from the sending group to the receiving one, so direction is drawn instead of read from two widths. Each group has its own hue and a ribbon takes the colour of its source group at reduced opacity; every ribbon carries "A to B: value (B to A: value)" (one direction when directed) in a hover title, and the hidden tables list every non-zero flow (from, to, value) and each group's total out and in; the aria label gives the number of groups, the total flow and the largest flow. Group names sit outside the ring, rotated to read outward and never upside down, shortened with an ellipsis where they do not fit and left out where a neighbour is too close (a visible legend always names every group). Motion-ready: every moving value reads --p (build progress 0 to 1, default 1) through a per-group --k, so a motion_timeline track on p builds it group by group and the standalone render is the finished picture; reduced motion shows the end state.
queries: show a chord_diagram: flows between a few entities as ribbons on a ring flows between a few entities in both directions as a circle: each group is an arc on the ring (its length is the flow render a chord diagram

name: Circle Pack
description: Part-to-whole as packed circles: each item is a circle whose area shows its value, and the optional per-item path (1 to 3 group names, top down) nests the circles inside outlined group circles, so a budget, a skills inventory or a folder tree reads as clusters. Laid out by d3-hierarchy pack() (circle packing: the front-chain placement of packSiblings and the smallest enclosing circle of packEnclose, padding 3) on the server, so there is no script. A group's hue follows its top-level group and a deeper circle is a lighter shade of it; group circles are outlined, leaf circles are filled. Every circle carries its name, path, value and share in a hover title and in the hidden table (item, path, value, share of total), and the aria label gives the total, the number of groups and the largest item. A leaf name (and its value, in a wider container) is drawn inside the circle where it fits, and a group name at the top of its circle where it fits; both are 12 px text gated on the container width. Motion-ready: every moving value reads --p (build progress 0 to 1, default 1) through a per-depth --k, so a motion_timeline track on p builds it level by level from the groups inward and the standalone render is the finished picture; reduced motion shows the end state.
queries: show a circle_pack: grouping and rough size as packed circles part-to-whole as packed circles: each item is a circle whose area shows its value, and the optional per-item path (1 render a circle pack

name: Arc Diagram
description: Connections between named things as arcs: the nodes sit on one horizontal line and each link is a semicircle above it joining its two nodes (the d3 gallery "arc diagram"), so a co-authorship list, a module-dependency graph or a who-talks-to-whom table reads as clusters of short arcs and a few long ones. Node positions are even steps along the line (d3-scale scalePoint with padding 0.5) and the arcs are static SVG, so there is no script. Arc thickness shows the link value (1 to 6 px; all links at 2 px when every value is equal). The optional node group sets the dot and the arc colour (an arc takes its source node's) and a legend names every group, but colour is never the only cue: every dot and arc carries its name, group, link count or value in a hover title, and the hidden tables list every node with its group and link count and every link with its two ends and value. The aria label gives the node and link counts and the most connected node. Node names hang below the line rotated 90 degrees; in a narrow container only every second, fourth or eighth name is drawn (the first always) so that none overlaps. Motion-ready: every moving value reads --p (build progress 0 to 1, default 1) through a --k, so a motion_timeline track on p draws the arcs and then the nodes and the standalone render is the finished picture; reduced motion shows the end state.
queries: show a arc_diagram: links between nodes as arcs over a line connections between named things as arcs: the nodes sit on one horizontal line and each link is a semicircle above it render a arc diagram

name: Contour Plot
description: Filled contour bands drawn from data: either a grid of values (a temperature, elevation or pressure field) or a cloud of points (the density of delivery locations, incidents or customers). Both use d3-contour: for a grid, marching squares at evenly spaced levels (d3's default count of levels, or the thresholds field); for points, a kernel density estimate (d3 contourDensity: the points are smoothed with the given bandwidth and contoured at up to 20 levels). Bands run from light to dark as the value or density rises, every band is named in a legend as a range of numbers (never colour alone), and a thin outline marks each level. A grid is drawn with column and row numbers on its axes; points use their own x and y with nice axis ticks and are also drawn as faint dots. Static SVG, no script, scaled to its container. The hidden tables give every level with its colour name and, for a grid, the share of cells at or above it, for points the share of points in cells at or above it, then the points themselves (first 200). The aria label gives the mode, the size, the value range and the number of levels. Motion-ready: each band reads --p through a --k so a motion_timeline track on p draws the bands from the lowest level up; the standalone render is the finished picture.
queries: show a contour_plot: filled contour bands of a value grid or of the density of points filled contour bands drawn from data: either a grid of values (a temperature, elevation or pressure field) or a cloud render a contour plot

name: Voronoi
description: Nearest-site regions of a set of points: the plot is split into one region per site, each region being every spot that is closer to its site than to any other site (a catchment or service area: which store, depot, sensor or office is nearest). Regions come from a Delaunay triangulation and its Voronoi cells (d3-delaunay, with delaunator and robust-predicates), clipped to the sites' extent plus a margin, with nice axis ticks in the data's own units. Each region is filled with a light colour by group (a legend names every group, never colour alone) or with one light fill and a visible outline when there are no groups; the site is a dot, and its label sits under the dot when the region is wide enough for it (otherwise the label is hidden; the full label is in the region's tooltip and in the table). Static SVG, no script, scaled to its container. The hidden table lists every site with x, y, group, value and its share of the area. The aria label gives the number of sites, the number of groups and the site with the largest region. Motion-ready: each region reads --p through a --k so a motion_timeline track on p fades the regions in one after another; the standalone render is the finished picture.
queries: show a voronoi: nearest-site regions of a set of points (catchments, service areas) nearest-site regions of a set of points: the plot is split into one region per site, each region being every spot that render a voronoi

name: Candlestick Chart
description: Price movement as open-high-low-close bars on a date axis, drawn on the server as static HTML with no script. With the default style "candle" each bar is a wick from low to high and a body from open to close; with style "ohlc" it is a stem with a tick to the left for the open and a tick to the right for the close. Direction never rests on colour alone: a bar that closes at or above its open is hollow (candle) or a thin bar (ohlc) in the --positive colour, one that closes lower is filled (candle) or a thick bar (ohlc) in the --negative colour, a legend says so in words, and the hidden table has a Direction column. Bars sit at their real dates (weekend gaps show as gaps), the date axis ticks and labels follow d3-scale scaleUtc and d3-time-format, and the price axis follows d3 nice() and ticks(). An optional volume panel under the price panel repeats the hollow or filled cue. A hidden table gives every value. Motion-ready: each bar fades in through --k from --p (build progress 0 to 1, default 1); the standalone render is the finished picture and reduced motion shows the end state.
queries: show a candlestick_chart: open-high-low-close price bars over time price movement as open-high-low-close bars on a date axis, drawn on the server as static html with no script. with the render a candlestick chart

name: Parallel Coords
description: Rows of numbers compared across 2 to 8 measures at once: each measure is a vertical axis with its own scale, and each row is one line that crosses every axis at its value, so clusters, trade-offs and outliers across many measures show as bundles of lines. Optionally the lines are coloured by one measure (a light-to-dark ramp from the theme accent, with a legend giving the range). Axis scales come from d3 scaleLinear nice() and ticks() and the lines from d3 line(), computed on the server, so there is no script. The picture is static: the interactive brushing of a Plotly parallel-coordinates chart (dragging on an axis to filter rows) is not available. A hidden table gives every value of every row.
queries: show a parallel_coords: compare many numeric measures per row rows of numbers compared across 2 to 8 measures at once: each measure is a vertical axis with its own scale, and each render a parallel coords

name: Ternary Plot
description: Shows what share each of three parts makes up of a whole, one dot per observation, on an equilateral triangle: a point's distance from a corner is how little of that part it has, and the corners are pure A, pure B and pure C. Values are normalised to shares that sum to 100%, gridlines run every 20% on all three axes with their percentages printed on the edges, and an optional dashed line joins the points in the order given. The axis ticks come from d3-scale's linear ticks and the placing is plain trigonometry, computed on the server, so there is no script. A hidden table gives every point's three shares. Static, settled picture; each point fades in through --k from --p (build progress 0 to 1, default 1).
queries: show a ternary_plot: three-part mixes as points on a triangle shows what share each of three parts makes up of a whole, one dot per observation, on an equilateral triangle: a render a ternary plot

name: Quiver
description: A field of arrows on linear axes: each arrow sits on its x, y point and points the way its u (across) and v (up) numbers say, with a length in proportion to the size of the vector. Use it for wind, flow, forces or any vector field. The axes come from d3 nice() and ticks() (d3-scale's linear scale), computed on the server, so there is no script. Arrows are centred on their point, drawn at a fixed size scale so the longest is a set length, and an arrow of length 0 is a dot. A hidden table gives every arrow's x, y, across, up and length. Static, settled picture; each arrow fades in through --k from --p (build progress 0 to 1, default 1).
queries: show a quiver: arrows showing direction and size at points a field of arrows on linear axes: each arrow sits on its x, y point and points the way its u (across) and v (up) render a quiver

name: Choropleth Map
description: A map of regions shaded by one number each: world countries, US states or European countries. Give a region_set and a list of {id, value}; the server shades every region in one of 3 to 9 equal-interval classes (steps, default 5), draws a legend of the class ranges and hatches the regions that have no value, so a gap never reads as a low number. Colours come from the theme tokens (sequential accent ramp, or a diverging accent2-to-accent ramp through a neutral middle); Viridis, Turbo and other fixed colour maps are not offered. The outlines are bundled with the catalogue (Natural Earth 1:110m for countries, US Census 1:10m for states): there is no custom GeoJSON, so a region that is not in the set cannot be added. A hidden table lists each region with its code, value and class, largest first, and the regions with no value are listed in a details element. A payload that breaks the rules shows a short note instead of a map.
queries: show a choropleth map: world, US states or Europe shaded by value in classes a map of regions shaded by one number each: world countries, us states or european countries. give a region_set and a render a choropleth map

name: Geo Map
description: Points and lines on a map: dots at latitude and longitude, optionally sized by a number and grouped, and great-circle lines between places, drawn over the same bundled outlines and projections as choropleth_map (world countries, US states or European countries; Equal Earth, Mercator or the US composite). Each group gets its own marker shape as well as its own colour, each line its own dash, so colour is never the only cue. A hidden table lists every point (including any that fall outside the frame, which are noted) and every line. A payload that breaks the rules shows a short note instead of a map.
queries: show a geo map: points sized and grouped by value, plus great-circle lines, on bundled outlines points and lines on a map: dots at latitude and longitude, optionally sized by a number and grouped, and great-circle render a geo map

name: Polar Chart
description: Points and lines placed by angle and distance from a centre: each series gives a radius r and an angle theta for every point, so a compass or wind bearing, a cyclic pattern (hour of day, month) or a radar of scores per category reads as a circular chart. Angles are degrees, or categories (any text) spread evenly around the circle, which draws a radar chart. Up to 6 series are drawn as lines, markers or both, each with its own dash and marker shape so no series depends on colour alone; the optional fill "toself" shades the closed shape of a series. The radial axis starts at 0 (or the lowest negative value) and ends at a round number d3 nice() picks, with circular gridlines at d3 ticks(); an explicit r_range sets it, and a point outside the range is not drawn and is counted in a note. Angles are turned to positions by d3-shape lineRadial() maths and scaled by a d3-scale linear scale, on the server, so there is no script. A large series is thinned to evenly spaced points (the first and last of the points read are kept) with a visible note, the same cap that stands in for Plotly's WebGL scatterpolargl; a series is read up to 5000 points and a longer one says so in a note, so no point is dropped without being counted. The hidden table lists every point with a Status column (drawn, or outside the radial range and not drawn), and the aria label gives the radial range of the drawn points, the categories and each series' extent. Motion-ready: each series fades in through --k from --p (build progress 0 to 1, default 1); the standalone render is the finished picture and reduced motion shows the end state.
queries: show a polar_chart: points and lines by angle and radius, or a radar points and lines placed by angle and distance from a centre: each series gives a radius r and an angle theta for every render a polar chart

name: Histogram2D
description: Counts of x,y points in a grid of 2-D bins (the Plotly histogram2d trace), drawn as a heatmap: d3 bin() is run once on x and once on y, the cell count is the number of points that fall in both bins, and the grid is handed to the heatmap atom, so it has the heatmap colour bar, the cell counts printed inside the cells and a hidden data table. The highest y bin is the top row. Use nbinsx and nbinsy for the number of bins (the real count is the nearest round step, as in d3), or leave them out for the Sturges default. At most 20,000 points are used and at most 40 bins per axis, each with a note.
queries: show a histogram2d: x,y points counted into a 2-D bin grid, drawn as a heatmap counts of x,y points in a grid of 2-d bins (the plotly histogram2d trace), drawn as a heatmap: d3 bin() is run once on render a histogram2d

name: Scatter Matrix
description: A scatter plot matrix (Plotly splom): 2 to 6 numeric dimensions on one grid, every dimension on a shared axis across its row and column, so each cell plots one dimension against another and a pattern between any two shows at a glance. Below the diagonal each cell is a small scatter plot of every complete row (the upper half too with show_upper); the diagonal names the dimension; wide pages also show each dimension's range on the outer edges. Each axis comes from d3 nice() and ticks() on the server, so there is no script. A legend lists every dimension with its range and a hidden table gives every value of every row. Static: no hover or brushing. Motion-ready: each cell fades in through --k from --p (default 1).
queries: show a scatter_matrix: every measure plotted against every other a scatter plot matrix (plotly splom): 2 to 6 numeric dimensions on one grid, every dimension on a shared axis across render a scatter matrix

name: Motion Transition
description: Morphs one atom into another on the film's progress dial p, joining their elements by data key: two views of the same data (a treemap and a sunburst, a table and an org chart) hand over element by element instead of cross-fading. Each element of the second block that shares a key with the first starts on its partner's box and travels to its own place; with path keys a total starts on the union of its parts (Cloud collects Cloud/VMs and Cloud/Storage) and a part starts on its total; elements only in one block fade. Labels only fade. With reduced motion, on static surfaces or when no timeline sets p, the page shows the second block exactly as it renders alone.
queries: show a a key-joined morph from one atom to another on the film's p dial morphs one atom into another on the film's progress dial p, joining their elements by data key: two views of the same render a motion transition

name: Motion Map3D
description: A tilted 3D city map built from CSS alone (perspective and a rotated plane: no WebGL, no map tiles, no fetch). Blocks stand on a ground plane as three-faced boxes, either a seeded generated city, explicit blocks, or generated district clusters (cities). Outlines of real-world countries or states can be drawn directly on the ground plane under the blocks and route. As p runs 0 to 1 the camera descends and tilts in (p 0 to 0.3), then one or more legs draw on from station to station (p 0.3 to 0.92, optionally bending in arcs and pausing at stations with dwell times) with each station going from idle to active as a leg reaches it and then to its own state (idle, active, done, warn or error), payload chips can travel along the legs, and an optional clock chip counts in clock time, seconds or milliseconds. Station pins and labels sit on their own layer above the city, so blocks never cover them. Made for journeys through a system as much as through a city: a request trace, an agent's tool call and its reply, a deploy pipeline, an incident. At p = 1 every leg is fully drawn, the stations are in their final states and the clock shows its end value.
queries: show a a tilted 3D city map where legs draw station to station (out and back, straight or curved), chips travel, stations end done, warn or error and a clock counts; for request traces, agent tool calls, pipelines and delivery routes a tilted 3d city map built from css alone (perspective and a rotated plane: no webgl, no map tiles, no fetch). blocks render a motion map3d

name: Guarding derived indicators (agent skill)

Fires before and during such arithmetic, even on single-dataflow cases that skip linkage and on intermediates never shown to a reader. Governs admissibility and caveats, not attribution or licensing, which is citing-official-statistics.

Fires when units combine for a ratio, share, difference, contribution, correlation or ranking, even when combining sources is unstated, for intermediate values never surfaced, and when series from different agencies or dataflows sit side by side.
